title: Dental Implant Treatment With Guided Bone Regeneration in a Patient With Active Crohn’s Disease Under Long -Term Immunosuppressive and Anti-inflammatory Therapy
authors: Chapanov, K., Stoeva, D. & Naydenov, A. Cureus 17, e83439 (2025).
supports: Clinical study from the botiss maxresorb / maxresorb inject (biphasic CaP) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Abstract, verbatim (no separate conclusion section): “This report presents a case of dental implant treatment with guided bone regeneration in a 46 -year-old patient with active Crohn's disease, who was undergoing long -term immunosuppressive therapy (azathioprine) and anti-inflammatory treatment (mesalazine). A titanium implant was placed six weeks after the extraction of tooth 22. Alveolar augmentation was performed using synthetic xenograft material in combination with a collagen membrane. Seven months later, a provisional restoration was delivered, followed by the placement of a definitive screw -retained crown 120 days afterward. No complications were reported throughout the treatment, and the patient consistently maintained 18 excellent oral hygiene. This case underscores the feasibility of implant therapy in immunocompromised patients, despite longstanding concerns regarding the potential negative impact of immunosuppressive agents o” This records what the paper says, not what a rep may say: the sales wording still has to pass the claim tiers, and a study in one indication licenses nothing in another.
